name: What Delays Commercial Construction Projects in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: What causes the biggest delays in commercial construction projects in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What causes the biggest delays in commercial construction projects in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Commercial construction delays in Los Angeles are often caused by a combination of preconstruction and field issues. Permit review and agency coordination can slow the start date, especially if drawings are incomplete or revisions are required. Once construction begins, scope changes, late material selections, utility conflicts, structural surprises, and specialty equipment lead times can all push the schedule. Tenant improvement projects are particularly vulnerable when ownership, tenant, and design teams are not aligned on the final scope. Site access, staging limitations, and neighboring business operations can also affect productivity. The best way to reduce delays is to complete design decisions early, clarify who is responsible for approvals, order long-lead items as soon as the design is fixed, and hold regular coordination meetings during the permit and construction phases. A contractor should provide a schedule that identifies critical path items, inspection milestones, and decision deadlines so the project stays predictable.
acceptedAnswer.description: The biggest delays usually come from permit review, design changes, utility coordination, long-lead materials, and hidden site conditions. Tenant improvement projects also slow down when scope decisions are not finalized early. Projects move faster when drawings are complete, approvals are coordinated, and material selections are locked in before construction starts.
